name: Earl LeRoy "Buddy" Carter
incumbencyStatus: challenger (currently U.S. Representative GA-01, 2015-present; sixth term; not seeking re-election to House)

biography.currentRole: U.S. Representative, Georgia's 1st Congressional District (2015-present); serves on House Budget Committee and Energy and Commerce Committee (chairs Health Subcommittee)
priorRoles: Owner and operator, Carter's Pharmacy Inc., southeast Georgia (30+ years)
biography.education: Associate degree, Young Harris College (1977); B.S. Pharmacy, University of Georgia (1980)
biography.background: Licensed pharmacist and small business owner. Self-describes as 'MAGA warrior.' Born 1957, Port Wentworth, Georgia. Coastal Georgia district based in Savannah.

campaignWebsite.notes: Campaign website exists at buddycarter.com; direct fetch not available. Content sourced from buddycarter.house.gov/issues/ (official House site) and news coverage of campaign announcements.

statedPositions.quote: Georgians deserve someone who will support the president and his America first policies, secure borders
statedPositions.notes: Campaign launch statement; also called for expanded ICE presence in Atlanta (Nov 2025). Voted for Secure the Border Act (2023).

statedPositions.quote: We don't have men participating in girls' sports
statedPositions.notes: Repeatedly cited as a top campaign priority in multiple interviews; primary campaign theme alongside border security.

statedPositions.quote: Donald Trump delivered one of the greatest economies in his first term that we've ever seen
statedPositions.notes: General alignment with Trump economic agenda; campaigning as full MAGA endorser.

statedPositions.quote: All-of-the-above energy approach, which begins with increasing domestic production of all forms of American energy
statedPositions.notes: From official House issues page. Supports fossil fuels, domestic production, and some renewables (has touted Hyundai EV plant in district).

statedPositions.quote: ACA should immediately be dismantled, repealed and replaced... market-driven solutions to our health care system
statedPositions.notes: Consistent across entire House career; voted against ACA 9 times. Prefers market competition over government price controls.

statedPositions.quote: Education decisions are best made by those closest to the student: families, teachers, and communities in states
statedPositions.notes: Supports local control, school choice legislation, and eliminating Common Core. Cosponsored National School Choice Week resolution.

statedPositions.quote: Efforts to expand gun control and restrict access to legal gun use have proven ineffective in reducing crime
statedPositions.notes: Strong gun rights supporter; NRA A-rated. Voted against Bipartisan Background Checks Act and Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (2022).

statedPositions.quote: The Fair Tax scraps the tax code, abolishes the IRS and eliminates all personal and corporate income taxes
statedPositions.notes: Introduced H.R. 25 FairTax Act of 2025 — signature legislative priority. Would replace all income taxes with 23% national sales tax.

statedPositions.quote: Medicaid is there to be a lifeline, not a lifestyle. Nearly $1 trillion in cuts will help stabilize Medicaid for future generations
statedPositions.notes: Led Medicaid cuts in One Big Beautiful Bill as Health Subcommittee Chair. Publicly said he would 'actually like to see more' than $880B in cuts.

statedPositions.quote: Supported the U.S. Supreme Court's decision in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization; believes abortion laws should be made by individual states
statedPositions.notes: A+ rating from SBA Pro-Life America. Voted to defund Planned Parenthood. Supports state-level determination rather than federal ban.

statedPositions.quote: PBMs would be able to bring competition to bear and really get the cost down for all of us
statedPositions.notes: As a pharmacist, favors market competition through PBM regulation over Medicare government price negotiation. Led PBM Reform Act provisions in 2026 spending bill.

votingRecord.attendanceRate: 97.3% (missed 164 of 6,160 roll call votes, Jan 2015-Feb 2026; on par with median 2.0%)

keyVotes.notes: Voted to fully or partially repeal ACA nine times. Called himself 'leader in crafting' Republican replacement plan. Consistent position since entering office.
Called it 'one of the proudest votes he took as a member of Congress.' Lowered corporate and individual tax rates.
Voted against universal background check requirement for all firearm sales.
Was among the 179 House Republicans who voted No. First major federal gun safety legislation in 30 years.
Voted against despite clean energy investments in his district (Hyundai EV plant). Later signed letters against 'sledgehammer' approach to IRA repeal, but said IRA repeal is 'not a red line' for him.
Carter described it as 'the strongest border security bill in House history.'

keyVotes.bill: 21st Century Peace through Strength Act / Foreign Aid (Israel, Ukraine, Taiwan) (2024)
keyVotes.notes: Supported $95B package for military aid. 'Peace through strength' framing. Broke from isolationist wing of party.

keyVotes.bill: Marijuana Opportunity Reinvestment and Expungement Act (2022)
keyVotes.notes: Voted against federal marijuana decriminalization and expungement.
Voted to decertify Pennsylvania's electoral votes. Maintained objection even after Capitol riot. Framed as constitutional concern over state election law changes, not outcome dispute.

Passed 218-214 on July 3, 2025. Carter was lead architect of Medicaid provisions as Health Subcommittee Chair. Bill included ~$1T in Medicaid cuts (CBO estimated 10.5M+ lose coverage by 2034), SNAP work requirements, and large tax cuts. Signed into law July 4, 2025.
Would abolish IRS and replace income/payroll/estate taxes with 23% national sales tax. Carter's flagship legislative priority.
Voted against codifying same-sex and interracial marriage protections.

scorecards.notes: Near-zero environmental voting record. Strongly opposed to major climate legislation. Voted against offshore drilling bans. Supports all-of-the-above fossil fuel approach.

Endorsed by NRA since initial 2014 House campaign. Voted against Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (2022) and Bipartisan Background Checks Act. Supports national right-to-carry reciprocity. A-grade indicates consistent pro-gun-rights voting record.
Trend toward higher conservative alignment scores over his House career. One of the more reliable conservative votes on fiscal and social issues.

Carter has sought Trump's endorsement and met with him at White House. Trump has not endorsed any candidate in Georgia Senate primary, reportedly to avoid intraparty conflict with also-running Rep. Mike Collins. Carter calls himself 'MAGA warrior' and has aligned vote with Trump agenda.
Major ally on PBM reform legislation. Carter speaks at NCPA events and champions pharmacist community interests.

positionConflicts.conflict: Voted against IRA in 2022, but then signed three Republican letters opposing a 'sledgehammer' approach to IRA repeal. Also said IRA repeal is 'not a red line' for him. Position driven by $7.6B Hyundai EV/battery plant investment in his coastal Georgia district.

Claims 'we're not kicking anyone off Medicaid' while publicly endorsing $880B+ in cuts that CBO projects will strip coverage from 10.5 million people by 2034. Led the committee crafting the cuts as Health Subcommittee Chair.

As a pharmacist and champion of PBM reform, Carter has fought to lower drug costs through market competition. Yet voted against the Inflation Reduction Act's Medicare drug price negotiation provisions. Favors market mechanisms; opposes government price-setting.

His House website has a press release supporting bipartisan criminal justice reform, but he voted against marijuana expungement (MORE Act) and opposes eliminating mandatory minimums. 'Bipartisan' reform framing appears narrow.

evidenceSummary.notes: 11-year House voting record (2015-present) provides extensive evidence. Carter's record is consistently conservative across most axes with high signal from LCV (4% lifetime), NRA (A-grade), Heritage Action (77-92% range), SBA Pro-Life (A+), and US Chamber (recurring Spirit of Enterprise). Genuine specialty expertise in pharmaceutical/PBM policy creates some nuance in healthcare cost control axis. The IRA position conflict is notable: voted against it but opposed full repeal due to district economic interests. FairTax advocacy is a signature differentiator. Housing is the major evidence gap. Self-styled 'MAGA warrior' identity is central to 2026 Senate campaign. As of Feb 2026, Carter trails in primary polling (11%) without Trump endorsement.
